mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 5.0 for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of > 2% 3-month GDPC1 decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of > 1% 3-month PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).
